```text
=== translate-pane-copy.toml
# herdr-plus Quick Action — translate the focused pane straight to the clipboard.
# Managed by chezmoi. Same capture pipeline as "Translate pane", but no viewer
# pane: the bilingual text goes to `x copy` and a notification reports the size.
# Use it when the destination is a chat/editor rather than your eyes.
# See docs/tools/herdr.md § "Translate a pane".
name = "Translate pane: copy"
description = "Bilingual translation of the current page, onto the clipboard"
command = "~/.config/herdr/pane-translate.sh visible \"$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID\" --copy"
=== translate-pane-to.toml
# herdr-plus Quick Action — translate the focused pane into a language you type.
# Managed by chezmoi. The form field becomes {{.Value}} and is passed as --to,
# which translate resolves fuzzily ("chinees" -> zh). Without it the target comes
# from translate's own [general] config (or $HERDR_TRANSLATE_TO).
# See docs/tools/herdr.md § "Translate a pane".
name = "Translate pane into…"
description = "Same as Translate pane, but pick the target language"
type = "form"
command = "~/.config/herdr/pane-translate.sh visible \"$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID\" --to '{{.Value}}'"

[form]
prompt = "Translate this pane into"
placeholder = "e.g. zh-TW, en, japanese"
=== translate-pane.toml
# herdr-plus Quick Action — translate the focused pane, with a scope picker.
# Managed by chezmoi. Runs ~/.config/herdr/pane-translate.sh against
# $HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID; it captures, cleans, splits a pane and renders a bilingual
# view there (Quick Actions have no PTY, so the viewer has to be a real pane).
#
# Scope: "current page" is --source visible, which is exactly what you are looking
# at — and on an alternate-screen agent pane (Claude Code) it is also ALL there is:
# rows that leave the alternate screen never enter herdr's host scrollback, so the
# recent:N options only pay off on shell/log/codex panes. 1000 is herdr's own hard
# per-read ceiling. Whatever you pick, HERDR_TRANSLATE_MAX_CHARS (12000) trims the
# capture to a boundary and the pane header reports the trim.
# See docs/tools/herdr.md § "Translate a pane".
name = "Translate pane"
description = "Bilingual view of this pane's content in a split pane"
type = "select"
command = "~/.config/herdr/pane-translate.sh {{.Value}} \"$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID\""

[[options]]
label = "Current page"
value = "visible"
description = "The on-screen viewport — what you are looking at right now"

[[options]]
label = "Last 200 lines"
value = "recent:200"
description = "Scrollback; top edge snapped to a block boundary"

[[options]]
label = "Last 500 lines"
value = "recent:500"
description = "Scrollback; trimmed to the character budget from the top"

[[options]]
label = "Last 1000 lines"
value = "recent:1000"
description = "herdr's hard per-read ceiling — there is no pagination past it"
=== open-repo.toml
```

```text
//
// Date: 2026-06-15
// Author: Spicer Matthews (spicer@cloudmanic.com)
// Copyright: 2026 Cloudmanic Labs, LLC. All rights reserved.
//

package main

import (
	"os"
	"os/exec"
)

// launchQuickActions is the Quick Actions action's entry point. herdr runs it
// server-side (from the plugin action / keybinding), so it has no terminal of its
// own. It captures the focused pane's context (working directory, workspace) from
// the env herdr injects, then asks herdr to open the action picker as a pane —
// overlay by default, or the placement set by [quick_actions].placement in
// config.toml — passing the encoded context along so the chosen command runs in
// the directory you launched from, not the picker's. herdr creates the pane and,
// when the picker exits, tears it down and restores your previous focus.
func launchQuickActions() {
	ctx := contextFromPluginEnv()
	enc, err := ctx.encode()
	if err != nil {
		errExit("could not encode run context:", err)
	}

	cfg, err := loadPluginConfig()
	if err != nil {
		errExit(err)
	}
	placement := resolvePlacement(cfg.QuickActions.Placement, "overlay")

	// HERDR_BIN_PATH points at the running herdr binary; it is the portable way to
	// call back into the CLI from a plugin command.
	herdr := os.Getenv("HERDR_BIN_PATH")
	if herdr == "" {
		herdr = "herdr"
	}

	args := []string{
		"plugin", "pane", "open",
		"--plugin", pluginID,
		"--entrypoint", paneEntrypoint("quick-actions-picker"),
		"--placement", placement,
		// Hand the launch context to the picker as a single shell-safe env var.
		"--env", "HERDR_PLUS_CTX=" + enc,
	}
	// IMPORTANT: do not add --cwd here. The manifest registers this pane with a
	// relative command (./bin/herdr-plus), which herdr resolves against the pane's
	// working directory — so the pane must run in the plugin's own install dir for
	// that path to resolve. Passing --cwd <launch dir> made herdr look for
	// ./bin/herdr-plus inside the launch directory and fail to spawn the picker.
	// The launch directory still reaches the picker — and the action it runs —
	// through HERDR_PLUS_CTX (ctx.WorkDir), which sets each command's cmd.Dir and
	// the per-repo action lookup. So --cwd was purely cosmetic; dropping it loses
	// nothing and matches how the projects pane (which never set it) already works.

	cmd := exec.Command(herdr, args...)
	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		errExit("could not open the quick-actions picker:", err)
	}
}
```

````text
## Quick Actions

A fuzzy launcher for one-off commands. Trigger it (action
`cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions`), fuzzy-pick an action, and it runs in the
directory you launched from. Actions are TOML files in the `quick-actions/` subdir
of [herdr-plus's config dir](#configuration) (seeded with editable examples on
first run). A repo can also ship its own in `<repo>/.herdr-plus/quick-actions/`, shown
under a **Project** heading above your **Global** ones — this repo ships
`make build` / `make test` as a live example.

There are three action types:

```toml
# command (default) — runs immediately
name = "GitHub"
command = "open https://github.com"
```

```toml
# select — pick from a second fuzzy list; the choice becomes {{.Value}}
name = "Open Repo"
type = "select"
command = "open https://github.com/cloudmanic/{{.Value}}"

[[options]]
label = "Herdr Plus"
value = "herdr-plus"
```

A select action can build its list at open time instead of hard-coding it. Set
`options_command` in place of `[[options]]` and it runs fresh every time the
action is picked, one option per line of stdout:

```toml
# select — options come from a command, so the list follows what is on disk
name = "New Project"
type = "select"
options_command = "ls -1 ~/projects"
command = "cd ~/projects/{{.Value}} && $EDITOR ."
```

`options_command` is templated exactly like `command`, so it can reference
`{{.WorkDir}}` and friends. A line becomes the option's label *and* value; add a
tab to give it a description — `herdr-plus\tinstalled` shows "installed" beside
the row without it ending up in `{{.Value}}`. If the command fails, the picker
shows the error as an unselectable row rather than an empty list.

```toml
# form — type a value that becomes {{.Value}}
name = "Search Google"
type = "form"
command = "open 'https://www.google.com/search?q={{.Value | urlquery}}'"

[form]
prompt = "Search Google for"
```

The `command` is a [Go template](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) rendered against
the launch context: `{{.WorkDir}}` (where you launched from), `{{.SessionTitle}}`
(the workspace label), `{{.Value}}` (select/form input), and more — also exported
as `HERDR_PLUS_*` environment variables. If a command doesn't reference
`{{.Value}}`, the value is appended as a final shell-quoted argument.

## Worktree auto-layout

herdr-plus can lay a project-style tab layout into a git **worktree** the moment
herdr creates *or opens* it. When you run `herdr worktree create`/`open` (or use
herdr's right-click worktree dialog), herdr makes a fresh workspace for the
worktree and fires a `worktree.created` event (new worktree) or `worktree.opened`
event (existing one); herdr-plus catches either, finds a layout matching the
worktree's repo, and opens that layout's tabs and panes in the new workspace —
every command running — with no keypress. This is the plugin system's `[[events]]`
hook (declared in [`herdr-plugin.toml`](herdr-plugin.toml)) put to work.

Layouts live in `~/.config/herdr-plus/worktrees/`, one TOML file per layout (the
file name doesn't matter). A layout is a `repo` matcher plus the same `[[tabs]]`
format projects use:

```toml
repo = "options-cafe"          # matches the worktree's repo name (case-insensitive)

[[tabs]]
name = "claude"
command = "claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --chrome"

[[tabs]]
name = "lazygit"
command = "lazygit"

[[tabs]]
name = "terminal"              # no command — just an empty shell
```

- **`repo`** (required) matches the new worktree's repository name — the repo's
````

```text
5:# Translate a herdr pane's terminal content with the `translate` CLI and show the
20:#   * `herdr pane read` caps at 1000 lines and has no offset/pagination flag, so
40:#                                              captures, splits a pane, and re-execs

104:lines = text.split("\n")
343:command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-translate: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
347:mode="visible"; pane=""; to=""; act="split"; pager="${PAGER:-less -R}"
378:    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
405:    raw=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$src" --format text --lines "$lines" 2>/dev/null) \
408:    raw=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$src" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
443:        herdr notification show "Translated $label" --body "$stats" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
447:        # We already own a PTY (popup / command pane): no split needed.
450:    split)
452:        # note it was taken BEFORE the split, because splitting narrows the source
454:        new=$(herdr pane split "$pane" --direction right --ratio 0.5 2>/dev/null \
456:            || { rm -f "$capture"; echo "pane-translate: split failed" >&2; exit 1; }
457:        [ -n "$new" ] || { rm -f "$capture"; echo "pane-translate: split returned no pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
462:            if herdr pane process-info --pane "$new" 2>/dev/null \
476:        herdr pane run "$new" "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
479:        # `pane split` has no --focus flag (PaneSplitParams.focus defaults false),
484:        ids=$(herdr pane get "$new" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane | "\(.workspace_id) \(.tab_id)"')
----
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# ~/.config/herdr/sidecar.sh — prefix+S command-pane launcher.
# Herdr creates/focuses a temporary right split; only undo its automatic zoom.
# Quitting Sidecar lets Herdr close the pane and restore the source focus/zoom.
set -eu

if [ "${HERDR_ENV:-}" != 1 ] || [ -z "${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}" ]; then
	printf '%s\n' 'sidecar: run this launcher from a Herdr command pane (prefix+S).' >&2
	exit 1
fi

herdr_bin=${HERDR_BIN_PATH:-herdr}

fail() {
	rc=$1
	shift
	printf 'sidecar: %s\n' "$*" >&2
	"$herdr_bin" notification show 'Sidecar could not open' --body "$*" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
	exit "$rc"
}

sidecar_bin=$(command -v sidecar) || fail 127 \
	'Sidecar is not installed. Enable installCodingAgents with dotcfg, then apply the configuration.'

# --current identifies this NEW pane, not HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the source).
"$herdr_bin" pane zoom --current --off >/dev/null || fail 1 'Could not show the Sidecar split.'

# The source live cwd is supplied by Herdr; quote it without shell evaluation.
exec "$sidecar_bin" --project "${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD:-$PWD}"
```

```text
claude-copilot() {
  local ss=run fast=0 prepared explicit_model launch_model fast_model env_json
  while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --fast) fast=1; shift ;;
      --no-specstory) ss=off; shift ;;
      --specstory) ss=run; shift ;;
      --specstory-mode)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || { printf '%s\n' '--specstory-mode needs run, exit or off' >&2; return 2; }
        ss="$2"; shift 2 ;;
      --specstory-mode=*) ss="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
      -h|--help)
        printf '%s\n' 'Usage: claude-copilot-once [--fast] [--specstory-mode run|exit|off] [claude args...]'
        printf '%s\n' '  Single-session CLI settings; claude-copilot is an identical spelling.'
        printf '%s\n' '  run (default): live recording; exit: sync after exit; off: no recording.'
        printf '%s\n' '  --specstory / --no-specstory are aliases for run / off.'
        printf '%s\n' '  Persistent project routing: copilot-here on'
        return 0 ;;
      *) break ;;
    esac
  done
  case "$ss" in run|exit|off) ;; *) printf '%s\n' "copilot: invalid recording mode: $ss" >&2; return 2 ;; esac
  if _copilot_claude_has_late_fast "$@"; then
    printf '%s\n' "claude-copilot: '--fast' must come before other arguments; refusing to forward it." >&2
    return 2
  fi
  if [ "$fast" -eq 1 ]; then
    local arg
    for arg in "$@"; do
      if [ "$arg" = -- ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "claude-copilot: --fast cannot be combined with '--' (the resolved --model would become prompt data)." >&2
        return 2
      fi
    done
  fi
  prepared="$(_copilot_session inspect claude "$ss" -- "$@")" || return $?
  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s\n' 'claude-copilot: jq is required' >&2; return 1; fi
  if ! _copilot_alive; then copilot-proxy start || return 1; fi
  _copilot_require_shim || return 1
  explicit_model="$(printf '%s' "$prepared" | jq -r '.model')"
  launch_model="$(_copilot_claude_fast_base_model "$explicit_model")" || return 1
  if [ "$fast" -eq 1 ]; then
    fast_model="$(_copilot_fast_model_for "$launch_model" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$fast_model" ]; then
      launch_model="$fast_model"
      prepared="$(printf '%s' "$prepared" | jq --arg model "$fast_model" '.argv += ["--model", $model] | .model = $model')" || return 1
      printf '%s\n' "claude-copilot: --fast -> $fast_model (session only)" >&2
    else
      printf '%s\n' "claude-copilot: --fast unavailable for $launch_model; using the standard model." >&2
    fi
  fi
  env_json="$(_copilot_env_json_for_model --live "$launch_model")" || return 1
  _copilot_session launch claude "$ss" "$prepared" "$env_json"
}

claude-copilot-once() { claude-copilot "$@"; }

3:`SpecStory` records terminal coding-agent sessions and can wrap supported agents with `specstory run`.
7:`specstory` is installed automatically by the `coding_agents` ansible role.
14:This dotfiles repo manages the user-level SpecStory config at `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`.
18:1. User-level config: `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`
19:2. Project-level config: `./.specstory/cli/config.toml`
20:3. CLI flags passed to `specstory`
22:Later sources override earlier ones. That means the dotfile provides global defaults, while a repo-specific `.specstory/cli/config.toml` can override them when a project needs different behavior.
25:    The user-level config is a chezmoi `create_` file (`private_dot_specstory/private_cli/create_config.toml`): chezmoi writes it on first `apply` and then **never touches it again**. This is deliberate — the SpecStory CLI writes runtime UI state back into the file (e.g. a `[resume]` block with `view_mode` / `last_agent` after `specstory resume`), which would otherwise show up as permanent chezmoi drift. To change the shipped defaults, edit the source and re-seed: `cp ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml)"`.
40:These are the commands `specstory run claude`, `specstory run codex`, and similar provider shortcuts will execute by default unless overridden per project or on the command line.
42:Codex 0.156.0 rejects the old `model_supports_reasoning_summaries` override and reports it as an ignored `session-flags` setting at startup. Keep `model_reasoning_summary="detailed"` to request detailed summaries. On existing hosts, remove only `-c model_supports_reasoning_summaries=true` from `codex_cmd` in `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` (and any project override); `chezmoi apply` does not update this seed-only file. Restart the Codex session to use the corrected command.
46:`<id>_cmd` controls **how** a provider launches, never **which** one bare `specstory run` picks. There is no `default_provider` key: with no argument, specstory resolves to the **alphabetically-first** entry of its provider registry. Adding `antigravity` in 2.9.0 therefore silently displaced `claude` as the default on every existing install, and `specstory run --help` re-generated itself to match (`By default, launches Antigravity CLI.`). Since `agy` was installed, the wrong agent launched successfully with no error.
48:Always write `specstory run claude`. This repo's wrappers do — see `_sesh_wrap_agent()` in `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` (shared by `scode` / `svibe` / `hcode` / `hvibe`) and [pitfalls/specstory-run-default-agent-drift.md](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/specstory-run-default-agent-drift.md).
```

```text
# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator.
#
# TRIAL config that mirrors the tmux experience as closely as herdr's
# primitives allow. herdr COEXISTS with tmux — you run one or the other (or
# nest deliberately; see docs/tools/herdr.md "nested inside tmux"). Nothing here
# touches the tmux / sesh / tmuxp / workmux setup.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE MANAGED BODY of a chezmoi modify_ overlay
# (dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl). The overlay enforces the tables
# below on every `chezmoi apply`. Herdr currently writes onboarding, update,
# theme/UI/sound/toast/pane-label/agent-sort, and key-reset changes; the overlay
# also preserves unrelated live/user-owned tables such as [session], [remote],
# and [experimental], whether or not Herdr writes them today.
#
# Schema: https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/
# Validate after editing: herdr server reload-config
# Full feasibility matrix + behavior model + documented gaps: docs/tools/herdr.md
#
# NOT gated by enableVimMode: that flag governs shell + tmux modal editing;
# herdr's copy mode (prefix+[) is vi-style natively (h/j/k/l, w/b/e, {/}, v, y).
#
# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux). herdr's built-in defaults are
# already close to tmux (prefix+c new tab, prefix+1..9 switch, prefix+h/j/k/l
# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,
# prefix+g session navigator, prefix+w workspace nav, prefix+q detach), so we
# only rebind a couple of keys and add command panes for the tv/dev/lazygit TUIs.
[theme]
name = "catppuccin"             # mocha (dark)
auto_switch = false             # keep Catppuccin Mocha regardless of terminal appearance
light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
dark_name = "catppuccin"
[ui]
mouse_capture = true
pane_borders = true
pane_gaps = true
confirm_close = true
show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true
status_indicators = "symbols" # distinct static glyphs for each agent state
# Agent sidebar ordering. herdr's default is "spaces" (grouped by space);
# "priority" turns the panel into an attention queue (blocked/waiting agents
# float to the top) instead of a per-space grouping. With many concurrent agent
# panes the queue is what you actually scan, so this is the more useful default
# here. Valid values: "spaces" | "priority" ("workspaces" is an alias for
# "spaces").
agent_panel_sort = "priority"
# Expanded Agent sidebar: keep workspace names on the first row, machine/agent
# on the second, and the task title without its activity glyph on the third.
# Empty titles disappear; machine is hidden when only Local is present.
# Keep `$review` for the review-pending star (prefix+m / hmark).
#
# Required since herdr 0.7.4: `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field
# were replaced by a namespaced token map, and unlike custom_status a token is
# rendered ONLY where a row layout names it — set a token with no layout entry
# and the flag silently exists in the API but shows up nowhere.
#
# Keep `$review` in sync with TOKEN in dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh.
# NOTE this pins the layout: upstream changes to the default rows will NOT reach
# us, so re-check this block against `herdr --default-config` on herdr upgrades.
[ui.sidebar.agents]
rows = [
  ["state_icon", "workspace", "tab", "$review"],
  ["machine", "agent"],
  ["terminal_title_stripped"],
]
[terminal]
shell_mode = "auto" # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd). Values:
#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
# NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live
# cwd — same as a split. herdr issue #912 changed `follow` so tabs behave like
# splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root" was treated as a bug and
# removed. NO new_cwd value opens a new tab at the WORKSPACE ("space") dir — for
# that use the prefix+C command below (derives the space root → tab create --cwd).
# See docs/tools/herdr.md.
new_cwd = "follow"
# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings (herdr docs), so a
# single action can carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
[keys]
split_vertical = [
  "prefix+|",
  "prefix+%",
] # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
split_horizontal = [
  "prefix+minus",
  "prefix+\"",
] # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
reload_config = "prefix+shift+r" # tmux: prefix+R
rename_tab = "prefix+," # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b" # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)
# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; add the workspace + agent analogs
# so a number key jumps directly, no navigate mode needed. The "N..M" range form
# is native herdr config syntax (same shape as switch_tab).
# NOTE on the modifier: prefix+SHIFT+digit does NOT work — under the kitty
# keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) shift+1 still carries the printable "!", so
# herdr matches the symbol, not "shift+1". ctrl+digit and alt+digit have no
# printable form, so they disambiguate cleanly. Hence ctrl (workspace) / alt (agent).
switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9" # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N (shift+N would emit !@#… — unusable)
focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"       # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane (herdr tracks agents per pane natively)
# --- Workspace navigate-mode: vim j/k (entered via prefix+w) ---
# prefix+w opens the workspace navigator; navigate_workspace_* are the
# navigate-mode-only movement keys. Add vim j/k alongside the default arrows so
# hjkl muscle memory carries here too. (These fields can't use prefix+/enter/tab/
# left/right or unmodified 1-9 — plain j/k are allowed.)
navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
navigate_workspace_up = ["k", "up"]
# --- Run an arbitrary command in a floating popup (prefix+E) ---
# The generalisation of the hardcoded prefix+G lazygit launcher: fzf-pick or type any
# command, run it in the FOCUSED PANE'S cwd, and the popup closes itself when the
# command exits. Helper: ~/.config/herdr/run-command.sh.
#
# type = "popup" (herdr >= 0.7.4) is the tmux `display-popup -E` analog: it floats
# ABOVE the tiled layout instead of splitting it, so nothing reflows and you land
# back exactly where you were. The same popup primitive powers scratch;
# prefix+G/Alt+g/btop/nvtop retain their temporary-pane forms.
#
# Deliberately not a herdr-plus Quick Action (prefix+y): Quick Actions run through
# `sh -c` with no PTY/stdin (the same reason btop/nvtop are command panes) and
# every action is a fixed command string with no free-text field.
#
```

```text
52:- Pane commands control raw terminals, shells, tests, servers, input, and output.
53:- Agent commands control the recognized coding agent currently occupying a pane.
55:A pane exists whether or not it contains an agent. `agent start` requires an existing available shell pane and never creates, splits, or moves layout. Use pane commands for ordinary processes. 57:Agent commands accept either a unique live agent name or the pane ID currently hosting that agent. They do not accept terminal IDs or bare agent-kind labels. Names must match `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}` and be unique among live agents. A name follows the current pane occupant and is cleared when that agent exits, is released, or is replaced.
59:`idle` and `done` both mean the agent is ready for input. The CLI/API uses the server's seen state to distinguish them; explicit focus commands mark the target seen, while reads do not. Each TUI client tracks viewed completions independently, so its Done badge can differ from the CLI or another client's badge. `blocked` means Herdr recognized an approval or question UI. `unknown` means an agent is present but Herdr cannot classify it confidently; it does not prove completion.
```

````markdown
# herdr: open a coding agent from Quick Actions and hotkeys

## Context
You want a fast way to open claude / codex / opencode / `claude-copilot-once` / `codex-copilot-once` from inside herdr, choosing (a) SpecStory recording or a direct run and (b) right split, down split, or new tab. Two things get in the way today. Splitting by hand starts a full zsh (about 0.3s), and then you still type the command. Copilot-once is a shell function in `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`, so it only exists in a shell that has loaded your full config.

**Menu limits (checked in the herdr-plus source, `action.go`).** The `Translate pane` screen you pointed to has two levels: the Quick Actions list, then one `select`. An `Option` has only `label/value/description/heading`, with no nested options, so a third level isn't possible. `heading` *does* render a dim group title, though. So the plan uses the Translate-pane shape:

- **Level 1** (the Quick Actions list, prefix+y): one action per agent, all named `Agent: …`. Typing `agent` filters to exactly these.
- **Level 2** (`select` with headings): the recording × placement combos, grouped under headings:
  ```
  SpecStory            ← heading
    → Split right
    ↓ Split down
    ⊞ New tab
  Direct               ← heading
    → Split right / ↓ Split down / ⊞ New tab
  ```
  OpenCode has no SpecStory provider, so it shows only the Direct group. The copilot variants map run/off to `--specstory-mode run|off`.

## Design

### 1. Launcher: `dot_config/herdr/executable_agent-open.sh` (new)
- Usage: `agent-open.sh <right|down|tab> <agent> <run|off>`, or `agent-open.sh last`.
- `agent` is checked against an allowlist: `claude codex opencode claude-copilot codex-copilot`. Nothing passed through is ever `eval`'d.
- Source pane is `$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID`, falling back to `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` and then `herdr pane current`. The cwd is `$HERDR_PLUS_WORKDIR`, then `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`.
- Splits use `herdr pane split <pane> --direction right|down --cwd … --focus --env HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH="<agent> <run|off>"`.
- Tabs use `herdr tab create --cwd … --label <agent> --focus --env HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH=…`.
- It writes the choice to `~/.cache/herdr/agent-open.last`, which is what `last` reads.
- On failure it calls `herdr notification show`, following the same pattern as `sidecar.sh` and `pane-translate.sh`.

### 2. Fast path in the rc files (top of `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, identical small block)
```sh
if [ -n "${HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH:-}" ]; then
  _hal=$HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH; unset HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH
  "$HOME/.config/herdr/agent-run.sh" $_hal   # child process; env changes don't leak
  unset _hal
fi   # then the normal rc continues → after the agent exits you get a fully loaded shell in the same pane
```
- The block goes in both rc files because the CLAUDE.md rules say both shells always deploy and must not be gated.
- It is placed before the oh-my-zsh, ble.sh and plugin init, so the bash 12-step init order is unaffected.
- `unset` runs first, so nested shells don't re-trigger it.

### 3. Lean runner: `dot_config/herdr/executable_agent-run.sh` (new, bash)
- Sources only what the agent needs:
  - `~/.config/shell/00_exports.sh` (PATH for `~/.local/bin` and `~/.opencode/bin`). A login shell lacks these; I checked.
  - mise PATH via `mise env -s bash`.
  - `~/.shellrc.secrets` and `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`, if present.
  - `43_copilot_proxy.sh`, only for the copilot agents. Sourcing it on its own works; I checked with `bash --norc`.
- It re-checks the allowlist, then maps the choice to a command:
  - `claude run` → `specstory run claude` (always names the agent explicitly; see pitfall `specstory-run-default-agent-drift`)
  - `claude off` → `claude`; `codex` works the same way
  - `opencode` → `opencode`
  - `claude-copilot run|off` → `claude-copilot-once --specstory-mode run|off`; `codex-copilot` works the same way
- Known gap, to be documented: the zsh-only `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh` is not loaded on the fast path.
- `HERDR_AGENT_FULL_RC=1` is an escape hatch. It sends the launcher down the slow path: split with no env, then `herdr pane run` into the fully loaded shell.

### 4. Quick Actions (new files under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/`)
- New files: `agent-claude.toml`, `agent-codex.toml`, `agent-opencode.toml`, `agent-claude-copilot.toml`, `agent-codex-copilot.toml`.
- Each one has `type = "select"` and `command = "~/.config/herdr/agent-open.sh {{.Value}}"`.
- Each option value has the form `right claude run`.
- Each file starts with a header comment, in the same style as `translate-pane.toml`.

### 5. Hotkeys (`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`, `[[keys.command]]`, `type = "shell"`, which is detached)
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `prefix+alt+c` | claude + SpecStory → split right |
| `prefix+alt+x` | codex + SpecStory → split right |
| `prefix+alt+t` | claude + SpecStory → new tab |
| `prefix+alt+r` | repeat last choice (`agent-open.sh last`) |

- These keys are free: the bound `prefix+alt+*` keys are only `1..9`, `a`, `e` and `f`.
- During implementation, verify that `type="shell"` receives `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`/`_CWD`. If it doesn't, fall back to `type = "pane"` with a script that exits right away.

### 6. Docs, tests and mirrors
- `docs/tools/herdr.md` and `herdr.zh-TW.md`: add a new § "Open a coding agent" covering the menu, the hotkeys, the fast path and the env gap.
- `docs/shells/keybindings.md`: add rows for the 4 keys.
- `dot_agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md.tmpl`: mention the herdr agent launcher and its keys, according to the CLAUDE.md "surfaced to agents" row.
- `tests/unit/herdr_agent_open.bats`: stub `herdr` on PATH in the style of `herdr_pane_translate.bats`, then assert:
  - the split/tab argv
  - allowlist rejection
  - the `last` round-trip
  - the agent-run command mapping, with `specstory`/`claude` stubbed

## Verification
- `bats tests/unit/herdr_agent_open.bats`.
- `chezmoi apply`, then `herdr server reload-config`. That command validates the config with the app itself.
- Manually in herdr:
  - prefix+y → type `agent` → Claude → SpecStory/Split right: the agent appears with no typed command. Quit it and a full shell prompt should follow.
  - Repeat with New tab, and with codex-copilot Direct.
  - Try each of the 4 hotkeys, and check that `prefix+alt+r` repeats the last choice.
- Timing: compare a fast-path split against prefix+v followed by typing `claude`.
- Run `zsh -i -c exit` and `bash -i -c exit` with no env set, to confirm the rc block is a no-op.
````

```text
# ~/.bashrc - Interactive bash configuration. Managed by chezmoi.
#
# Init order (load-bearing — see docs/shells/bash.md):
#   1.  Early-return guard (non-interactive shells)
#   2.  /etc/bashrc source (RHEL families)
#   3.  ble.sh --attach=none   ← BEFORE bash-preexec / starship
#   4.  XDG dirs + Homebrew shellenv (mac)
#   5.  Bash-specific config files (history / completion / vi-mode / aliases)
#   6.  oh-my-bash source (after ble.sh so OMB's bash-preexec install no-ops)
#   7.  Shared modular layer (starship / mise / zoxide / direnv / thefuck)
#   8.  atuin init bash --disable-up-arrow (ble.sh handles up-arrow history)
#   9.  Secrets
#   10. ble-attach   ← absorbs all precmd/preexec stacks accumulated above
#   11. ~/.bash_aliases (Debian/Ubuntu) + ~/.bashrc.d/* (RHEL family)
#       — backward-compat with distro skel conventions
#   12. .bashrc.adhoc tail (chezmoi-ignored; highest-priority user override)
#
# The ble.sh / oh-my-bash / atuin steps are presence-gated and no-op
# silently when the artefact isn't installed (e.g. fresh host before
# `chezmoi apply` finishes the externals + run-onchange-after_install).
# Plain bash without ble.sh + OMB still gets a fully working starship
# prompt + the shared layer + bash-completion v2.

# 1. ============================================================
# Non-interactive shells (SSH commands, cron, scp) bail out here.
# Anything below this guard runs only in interactive bash.
# Mirrors /etc/skel/.bashrc convention on Debian/Ubuntu.
case $- in
    *i*) ;;
      *) return ;;

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Unit tests for dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-translate.sh — the text pipeline
# behind the "Translate pane" Quick Actions and direct helper invocations.
# prefix+t opens the interactive TUI.
#
# Why this file earns its keep: the helper spends money. Every regression in the
# capture filter either sends terminal chrome to an LLM (waste) or silently sends
# nothing translatable (the dedent bug below). Both are invisible from the output
# of a successful run, so they have to be pinned here.
#
# Two behaviours in particular are non-obvious and have already bitten:
#
#   1. THE MODAL DEDENT. translate's bitext classifies a block as *code* once its
#      indent is >= base + 2. An agent pane renders prose behind a uniform left
#      margin while turn markers sit at column 0, so a min()-based base dedents
#      nothing and the ENTIRE page comes back untranslated — a successful,
#      billed, useless call. The base must be the MODAL indent.
#   2. `visible` IS NEVER TRIMMED AT THE TOP. It is literally what the user is
#      looking at; only `recent:N` windows may be snapped to a block boundary.
#
# The fixtures are shared with the Windows port: tests/fixtures/herdr/* here and
# the identical copies under dotfiles-windows/tests/fixtures/herdr/ are asserted
# byte-for-byte by tests/HerdrPaneTranslate.Tests.ps1 there. Regenerate an
# expectation with:
#   ./dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-translate.sh <mode> --dry-run < fixture
# only after convincing yourself the NEW output is the correct one.

load "../test_helper.bash"

setup() {
  HELPER="$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-translate.sh"
  FIX="$REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/herdr"
}

# The filter is an embedded python3 program inside the sh helper; run it directly
# so these tests need neither a herdr server nor the translate binary.
run_filter() { # MODE BUDGET < stdin
  local prog
  prog=$(sed -n '/^PY_FILTER=\$(cat <<.PY.$/,/^PY$/p' "$HELPER" | sed '1d;$d')
  python3 -c "$prog" "$1" "${2:-12000}" 2>/dev/null
}

@test "helper is valid POSIX sh" {
  run sh -n "$HELPER"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "visible: strips bottom chrome, dedents by the modal indent, keeps content" {
  output=$(run_filter visible < "$FIX/pane-capture.txt")
  [ "$output" = "$(cat "$FIX/pane-capture.visible.expected")" ]
}

@test "visible: the status-line block, prompt row and spinner are all gone" {
  output=$(run_filter visible < "$FIX/pane-capture.txt")
  [[ "$output" != *"Tokens 4.6M"* ]]
  [[ "$output" != *"bypass permissions"* ]]
  [[ "$output" != *"~statistics.json"* ]]
  [[ "$output" != *"Percolating"* ]]
  [[ "$output" != *"Context    "* ]]
}
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# ~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh
# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Open a NEW TAB rooted at the WORKSPACE ("space") directory, NOT the focused
# pane's live cwd.
#
# Why this exists: on herdr >=0.7.x, `new_cwd = "follow"` makes a new tab inherit
# the FOCUSED pane's cwd — herdr issue #912 (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912)
# changed `follow` so new tabs behave like pane splits, and the older "new tab
# opens at the workspace's initial dir" was treated as a bug and removed. There
# is NO new_cwd value for "workspace dir", so we compute it and pass it via
# `herdr tab create --cwd`. (herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field either —
# `herdr workspace get` has no cwd — so it must be derived.)
#
# "Space dir" = the cwd of the workspace's OLDEST surviving tab. That derivation
# is NOT inlined here: it lives in the sibling ~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh,
# shared with `pane-copy.sh dir` (prefix+y Quick Action) and the herdr-sesh tv
# channel. Change it there, once — including the caveat about the sidebar label
# drifting from it.
#
# Bound to prefix+C (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). prefix+c and the mouse
# "+" button keep herdr's native follow-the-focused-pane behavior. Uses the
# keybind-context $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (falls back to ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID).
#
# Usage:
#   new-tab-at-space-root.sh [pane_id]   # pane_id defaults to the current pane
set -eu

command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }

pane="${1:-${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}}"
[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: no pane id (pass one, or run inside herdr)" >&2; exit 64; }

wid=$(herdr pane get "$pane" | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // ""')
[ -n "$wid" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: could not resolve workspace for pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }

# Root dir derivation is shared — see space-root.sh. Resolve it beside this
# script rather than via PATH: a herdr command-pane may run us without the
# interactive PATH.
here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
root=$("$here/space-root.sh" "$wid") || exit 1

exec herdr tab create --workspace "$wid" --cwd "$root" --focus
```

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# ~/.config/herdr/agent-open.sh
# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_agent-open.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Open a coding agent in a new split or tab next to the focused herdr pane.
# Driven by the "Agent: …" Quick Actions (prefix+y) and the prefix+alt+c/x/t/r
# hotkeys (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml).
#
# Why the env var instead of `herdr pane run`: herdr can only spawn a pane with
# the default shell, and typing a command into it waits for the full interactive
# rc (~0.3s+). Instead the new pane's shell gets HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH, and a guard
# at the very top of ~/.zshrc / ~/.bashrc hands it to ~/.config/herdr/agent-run.sh
# BEFORE the heavy init — the rest of the rc runs after the agent exits, so the
# pane falls back to a normal shell. HERDR_AGENT_FULL_RC=1 opts out (slow path:
# plain split, then `herdr pane run` into the fully loaded shell).
#
# Only allowlisted tokens are forwarded; agent-run.sh re-checks them and never
# evals anything. See docs/tools/herdr.md § "Open a coding agent".
#
# Usage:
#   agent-open.sh <right|down|tab> <agent> <run|off>
#   agent-open.sh last            # repeat the previous choice
#   agent:  claude codex opencode claude-copilot codex-copilot
#   record: run = SpecStory live recording, off = direct
set -eu

herdr_bin=${HERDR_BIN_PATH:-herdr}
state="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/herdr/agent-open.last"

fail() {
	rc=$1
	shift
	printf 'agent-open: %s\n' "$*" >&2
	"$herdr_bin" notification show 'Agent launcher' --body "$*" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
	exit "$rc"
}

if [ "${1:-}" = last ]; then
	[ -r "$state" ] || fail 1 'No previous agent choice yet — pick one from prefix+y first.'
	# shellcheck disable=SC2046 # the state file holds three allowlisted words
	set -- $(cat "$state")
fi

[ "$#" -eq 3 ] || fail 64 'usage: agent-open.sh <right|down|tab> <agent> <run|off> | last'
placement=$1 agent=$2 record=$3

case "$placement" in right | down | tab) ;; *) fail 64 "unknown placement: $placement" ;; esac
case "$agent" in claude | codex | opencode | claude-copilot | codex-copilot) ;; *) fail 64 "unknown agent: $agent" ;; esac
case "$record" in run | off) ;; *) fail 64 "unknown record mode: $record" ;; esac
# SpecStory has no OpenCode provider — normalise instead of failing.
[ "$agent" = opencode ] && record=off

command -v "$herdr_bin" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 127 'herdr not found'
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 127 'jq is required'

# Quick Actions export HERDR_PLUS_*; keybindings export HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*.
pane=${HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID:-${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}}
[ -n "$pane" ] || pane=$("$herdr_bin" pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || :)
[ -n "$pane" ] || fail 1 'Could not find the source pane.'
cwd=${HERDR_PLUS_WORKDIR:-${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD:-$PWD}}

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$state")"
printf '%s %s %s\n' "$placement" "$agent" "$record" >"$state"

launch="$agent $record"
full_rc=${HERDR_AGENT_FULL_RC:-0}
set -- --cwd "$cwd" --focus
[ "$full_rc" = 1 ] || set -- "$@" --env "HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH=$launch"

if [ "$placement" = tab ]; then
	wid=$("$herdr_bin" pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || :)
	[ -n "$wid" ] && set -- --workspace "$wid" "$@"
	out=$("$herdr_bin" tab create --label "$agent" "$@") || fail 1 'herdr tab create failed'
	new=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
else
	out=$("$herdr_bin" pane split "$pane" --direction "$placement" "$@") || fail 1 'herdr pane split failed'
	new=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
fi

if [ "$full_rc" = 1 ]; then
	[ -n "$new" ] || fail 1 'herdr returned no pane id'
	"$herdr_bin" pane run "$new" "$HOME/.config/herdr/agent-run.sh $launch" >/dev/null || fail 1 'herdr pane run failed'
fi
```

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ~/.config/herdr/agent-run.sh
# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_agent-run.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# Run a coding agent with a LEAN environment — the fast path behind
# ~/.config/herdr/agent-open.sh. The HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH guard at the top of
# ~/.zshrc / ~/.bashrc calls this BEFORE oh-my-zsh / ble.sh / starship / atuin
# load, as a child process, so nothing here leaks into the shell that the pane
# falls back to once the agent exits.
#
# Loaded: shared exports (PATH incl. ~/.local/bin, ~/.opencode/bin), the editor
# vars, the cwd's mise env, the POSIX + bash secrets files, and — for the copilot
# agents only — 43_copilot_proxy.sh, which defines claude/codex-copilot-once.
# NOT loaded: ~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh (zsh syntax) and every interactive-only
# module. Need the exact interactive env? HERDR_AGENT_FULL_RC=1 on agent-open.sh.
#
# Usage: agent-run.sh <agent> <run|off>
#   agent: claude codex opencode claude-copilot codex-copilot
#   run = SpecStory live recording, off = direct

agent=${1:-} record=${2:-off}
case "$agent" in claude | codex | opencode | claude-copilot | codex-copilot) ;; *)
	printf 'agent-run: unknown agent: %s\n' "$agent" >&2
	exit 64
	;;
esac
case "$record" in run | off) ;; *)
	printf 'agent-run: unknown record mode: %s\n' "$record" >&2
	exit 64
	;;
esac

shell_dir="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/shell"
for f in "$shell_dir/00_exports.sh" "$shell_dir/09_editor.sh" \
	"$HOME/.shellrc.secrets" "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/bash/secrets.sh"; do
	# shellcheck disable=SC1090
	[ -r "$f" ] && . "$f"
done
if command -v mise >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	eval "$(mise env -s bash 2>/dev/null)"
fi

case "$agent" in
claude | codex)
	# Always name the provider: bare `specstory run` picks the alphabetically
	# first provider (pitfalls/specstory-run-default-agent-drift.md).
	if [ "$record" = run ]; then
		specstory run "$agent"
	else
		"$agent"
	fi
	;;
opencode) opencode ;;
claude-copilot | codex-copilot)
	# shellcheck disable=SC1091
	. "$shell_dir/43_copilot_proxy.sh" || exit 1
	"$agent-once" --specstory-mode "$record"
	;;
esac
```

```text
# Shared helpers for bats tests. Source from each .bats file:
#   load "../test_helper.bash"   # or the equivalent relative path
#
# Keep this file tiny. No bats-assert / bats-file / bats-support — plain
# bats built-ins ([ ], run, $status, $output) are enough.

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/.." && pwd)"
if [ "$(basename "$REPO_ROOT")" = "tests" ]; then
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT/.." && pwd)"
fi
export REPO_ROOT

_BATS_STUB_DIRS=()

# Create a temp directory and prepend it to PATH. Exposes the path via
# $BATS_STUB_DIR (not via stdout) so the PATH export actually sticks — using
# command substitution would run this in a subshell and discard the export.
setup_path_stub() {
  BATS_STUB_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bats-stub.XXXXXX")"
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS+=("$BATS_STUB_DIR")
  PATH="$BATS_STUB_DIR:$PATH"
  export PATH BATS_STUB_DIR
}

# Cleanup function. Call from your own teardown() if you override it:
#   teardown() { your_cleanup; cleanup_path_stubs; }
cleanup_path_stubs() {
  local dir
  for dir in "${_BATS_STUB_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -d "$dir" ] && rm -rf "$dir"
  done
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS=()
}

# Default teardown — fires only if the .bats file does not define its own.
teardown() { cleanup_path_stubs; }
tests/unit/herdr_edit_config.bats
tests/unit/herdr_focus_pane.bats
tests/unit/herdr_skill.bats
tests/unit/herdr_grep.bats
```

```bats
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Offline tests for the herdr coding-agent launcher pair:
#   dot_config/herdr/executable_agent-open.sh  (split/tab + HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH)
#   dot_config/herdr/executable_agent-run.sh   (lean env → agent command)
# plus the rc fast-path guard and the "Agent: …" Quick Action option values.
# The values are the wire format between the TOML files and the launcher: a
# typo there only shows up as a notification at click time, so pin it here.

load "../test_helper.bash"

OPEN="$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/herdr/executable_agent-open.sh"
RUN="$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/herdr/executable_agent-run.sh"
QA_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions"

setup() {
  setup_path_stub
  HERDR_LOG="$BATS_STUB_DIR/herdr.log"
  RUN_LOG="$BATS_STUB_DIR/run.log"
  export HERDR_LOG RUN_LOG
  export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR/cache"
  export HERDR_BIN_PATH="$BATS_STUB_DIR/herdr"
  export HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID=w1:p1 HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD=/src
  unset HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID HERDR_PLUS_WORKDIR HERDR_AGENT_FULL_RC
  cat > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/herdr" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
{ for a in "$@"; do printf '%s\t' "$a"; done; printf '\n'; } >> "$HERDR_LOG"
case "$1 $2" in
  "pane get")   echo '{"result":{"pane":{"pane_id":"w1:p1","workspace_id":"w1","cwd":"/live"}}}' ;;
  "pane split") echo '{"result":{"pane":{"pane_id":"w1:p9"}}}' ;;
  "tab create") echo '{"result":{"tab":{},"root_pane":{"pane_id":"w1:p8"}}}' ;;
esac
EOF
  # agent-run stubs: record the argv each "agent" was started with.
  for t in specstory claude codex opencode mise; do
    printf '#!/bin/sh\n[ "$(basename "$0")" = mise ] && exit 0\necho "$(basename "$0") $*" >> "$RUN_LOG"\n' > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/$t"
  done
  chmod +x "$BATS_STUB_DIR"/*
}

@test "scripts parse" {
  sh -n "$OPEN"
  bash -n "$RUN"
}

@test "split right: source pane, cwd and launch env reach herdr" {
  run "$OPEN" right claude run
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -q $'^pane\tsplit\tw1:p1\t--direction\tright\t--cwd\t/src\t--focus\t--env\tHERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH=claude run\t$' "$HERDR_LOG"
}

@test "Quick Action context wins over keybinding context" {
  HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID=w2:p3 HERDR_PLUS_WORKDIR=/qa run "$OPEN" down codex off
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -q $'^pane\tsplit\tw2:p3\t--direction\tdown\t--cwd\t/qa\t' "$HERDR_LOG"
}

@test "no cwd env: falls back to the pane's live cwd from herdr" {
  unset HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD
  run "$OPEN" right claude run
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -q $'\t--cwd\t/live\t' "$HERDR_LOG"
}

@test "tab: created in the source workspace, labelled with the agent" {
  run "$OPEN" tab codex-copilot run
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -q $'^tab\tcreate\t--label\tcodex-copilot\t--workspace\tw1\t--cwd\t/src\t--focus\t--env\tHERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH=codex-copilot run\t$' "$HERDR_LOG"
}

@test "opencode is normalised to off (no SpecStory provider)" {
  run "$OPEN" right opencode run
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -q 'HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH=opencode off' "$HERDR_LOG"
}

@test "unknown tokens are rejected before anything is spawned" {
  run "$OPEN" right 'claude;rm' run
  [ "$status" -eq 64 ]
  run "$OPEN" left claude run
  [ "$status" -eq 64 ]
  ! grep -q 'split' "$HERDR_LOG"
}

@test "last repeats the previous choice; fails cleanly before the first one" {
  run "$OPEN" last
  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
  "$OPEN" down codex run
  : > "$HERDR_LOG"
  run "$OPEN" last
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  grep -q $'--direction\tdown\t.*HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH=codex run' "$HERDR_LOG"
}

@test "HERDR_AGENT_FULL_RC=1: no env, command typed into the new pane" {
  HERDR_AGENT_FULL_RC=1 run "$OPEN" right claude off
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  ! grep -q HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH= "$HERDR_LOG" || grep -q $'^pane\trun\tw1:p9\t.*agent-run.sh claude off' "$HERDR_LOG"
  grep -q $'^pane\trun\tw1:p9\t' "$HERDR_LOG"
}

@test "agent-run maps choices to commands (specstory names the provider)" {
  HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR/cfg" "$RUN" claude run
  HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR/cfg" "$RUN" codex off
  HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$BATS_STUB_DIR/cfg" "$RUN" opencode off
  [ "$(cat "$RUN_LOG")" = "$(printf 'specstory run claude\ncodex \nopencode ')" ]
}

@test "agent-run rejects unknown agents" {
  run "$RUN" 'bash -c' off
  [ "$status" -eq 64 ]
}

@test "rc guard is present in both shells, before the heavy init" {
  grep -q 'agent-run.sh" ${=_herdr_agent_launch}' "$REPO_ROOT/dot_zshrc.tmpl"
  grep -q 'agent-run.sh" $_herdr_agent_launch' "$REPO_ROOT/dot_bashrc.tmpl"
  z_guard=$(grep -n HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH "$REPO_ROOT/dot_zshrc.tmpl" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  z_omz=$(grep -n '^plugins=(' "$REPO_ROOT/dot_zshrc.tmpl" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ "$z_guard" -lt "$z_omz" ]
  b_guard=$(grep -n HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH "$REPO_ROOT/dot_bashrc.tmpl" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  b_ble=$(grep -n 'ble.sh' "$REPO_ROOT/dot_bashrc.tmpl" | grep -v '^[0-9]*:#' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ "$b_guard" -lt "$b_ble" ]
}

@test "every Quick Action option value is a valid launcher argv" {
  vals=$(python3 -c '
import glob, sys, tomllib
for f in sorted(glob.glob(sys.argv[1] + "/agent-*.toml")):
    d = tomllib.load(open(f, "rb"))
    assert d["command"] == "~/.config/herdr/agent-open.sh {{.Value}}", f
    for o in d["options"]:
        if "value" in o: print(o["value"])
' "$QA_DIR")
  [ -n "$vals" ]
  while read -r p a r; do
    : > "$HERDR_LOG"
    "$OPEN" "$p" "$a" "$r"
  done <<< "$vals"
}
```

```text
## Keybindings

Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.

> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.

> **Pane env is frozen at herdr-server start.** Unlike tmux (`update-environment`), herdr does **not** refresh `SSH_CONNECTION` / `DISPLAY` / `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` / `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` on a new client attach — every pane inherits whatever the daemon had when it first started. Practical fallout: over SSH a pane's `$SSH_*` is empty while `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` still points at a stale local display, so clipboard tools that pick a backend by those vars copy to the wrong machine. `x` and Neovim work around it by keying on `HERDR_ENV` (→ OSC 52 via the pane TTY, which *does* proxy to the real client). Neovim deliberately uses that path for **copy only**: Herdr does not forward OSC 52 clipboard-query responses, so a full `unnamedplus` provider makes ordinary `p` wait for up to ten seconds. Use normal `p` for editor registers and terminal paste for inbound clipboard text. See [`pitfalls/x-copy-over-ssh-writes-remote-clipboard-not-osc52.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/x-copy-over-ssh-writes-remote-clipboard-not-osc52.md), [`pitfalls/nvim-p-waits-for-osc52-response-in-herdr.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/nvim-p-waits-for-osc52-response-in-herdr.md), and [clipboard.md](clipboard.md). For an agent forwarded via `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, re-export it per pane or start the server from a session that has it.

| Key | Action | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
| `prefix + C` | new tab at the workspace (**space**) root dir — `prefix+c` + mouse "+" stay follow-focused-pane | command pane |
| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + %` · `prefix + minus` / `prefix + "` | split side-by-side / stacked (tmux muscle memory — both the intuitive key and the tmux default) | rebound (arrays) |
| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator ([in-popup keys](#navigator-keys)) | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
| `prefix + ctrl + 1..9` | jump directly to **workspace** N (`switch_workspace`) | rebound (indexed) |
| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |

> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.
| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
| `prefix + Alt + e` | edit only the active runtime config, validate it, and reload (never invokes chezmoi) | command pane |
| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
| `prefix + d` | [`dev`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli) repository/task/worktree dashboard | command pane |
| `prefix + G` / `Alt + g` | lazygit temporary pane (a near-full popup was rejected because it blocks tab/workspace switching until closed) | command pane |
| `prefix + S` | [Sidecar](td_sidecar.md) to the right of the focused pane, 50/50, in its current directory; focus moves to Sidecar | command pane |
| `prefix + Y` | [Yazi](yazi.md) file manager rooted at the focused pane cwd; `q` returns to the unchanged layout | 90% × 85% popup |
| `prefix + M` | btop system monitor | command pane |
| `prefix + N` | nvtop GPU monitor | command pane |
| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
| `` prefix + u `` | **URL picker** — fzf-pick a URL from the pane and open it (`x open`); tmux-fzf-url analog. `--source recent` = full scrollback | command pane |
| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-panes` (non-shell / agent / process / shell panes) | command pane |
| `prefix + Alt + A` | `tv agent-wakeup` (dual-backend quota waits + scheduled continue) | command pane |
| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
| `prefix + Alt + F` | prompt for pane-content pattern → `herdr-grep --pick --visible` → fzf exact jump; Alt+S = scrollback, Alt+V = visible | command pane |
| `prefix + m` | toggle **review-pending** flag (⭐) on the current pane | command pane |
| `prefix + i` | `tv herdr-review` — review-pending **inbox** (flagged panes) | command pane |
| `` prefix + p `` | **copy a file path** from the pane — two-tier fzf (paths that exist under the pane cwd on top), copies the resolved absolute path (`x copy`) | command pane |
| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command popup |
| `prefix + E` | **run any command** in the pane's cwd — fzf-pick from history or type it; the popup closes itself when the command exits ([details](#run-any-command)) | command **popup** |
| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
| `` prefix + t `` | **interactive translator** — enter or paste text into the `translate` TUI ([details](#translate-pane)) | 80% × 80% popup |
| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |

> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`; many are built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above, while `prefix+Y` is unused upstream; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.

The direct lazygit shortcut uses lowercase `alt+g` (no prefix); `alt+G` would require `Alt+Shift+g`. Ghostty/cmux sends the configured Meta key from **Left Option** (`macos-option-as-alt = left`).

### Interactive popup and pane-translation Quick Actions

Same split as [`prefix + E`](#run-any-command): Quick Actions run through `sh -c` with **no PTY/stdin**, so they cannot host the pager themselves — they capture first, then `herdr pane split` a real pane and re-exec the helper inside it (`pane split` has no `--focus` flag, so the new pane is focused via the shared `focus-pane.py`). The direct `prefix+t` popup supplies a PTY for the interactive translator. For pane-translation Quick Actions, the capture is always taken **before** the split so that resizing cannot re-wrap the page being captured.

Lowercase `t`, because `prefix + T` is already the `herdr-sesh` session picker.

## AI usage / quota status
### 互動式 popup 與 pane 翻譯 Quick Actions

和 [`prefix + E`](#run-any-command) 是同一個分工：Quick Actions 透過 `sh -c` 執行、**沒有 PTY/stdin**，因此無法自己承載 pager——它們改成先擷取，再 `herdr pane split` 開一個真正的 pane 並在裡面重新執行 helper（`pane split` 沒有 `--focus` 參數，所以由共用的 `focus-pane.py` 負責 focus）。`prefix+t` 的 popup 直接提供互動式翻譯器需要的 PTY。Pane 翻譯 Quick Actions 則**一律在分割之前**完成擷取，避免縮小來源 pane 時重新換行而改變擷取內容。

用小寫 `t`，因為 `prefix + T` 已經是 `herdr-sesh` session 選擇器。

Pane 翻譯 helper 的環境變數（不適用於直接開啟的 `prefix+t` TUI）：`HERDR_TRANSLATE_MAX_CHARS`（12000）、`HERDR_TRANSLATE_TO`（預設目標語言；未設定時由 `translate` 自己的 `[general]` 設定決定）、`HERDR_RUN_HOLD`（`fail`|`always`|`never`，與 `prefix+E` 相同）、`PAGER`。

| **Static viewer** | `bindings` | zsh & bash (POSIX function in `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`) | Picks `tv` → `bat` → `less` → `cat` in that order; safe in non-interactive `bash -c` too |

Multiplexer bindings live in their own namespaces: tmux opens the quota wakeup
dashboard with `prefix + M-a`, while Herdr uses `prefix + Alt+A`. Both launch
the same `tv agent-wakeup` channel; neither chord shadows an inner-shell key.
```

````text
## herdr-plus plugin（sesh + tmuxp + menu 的對應物）

[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) 加了 **Projects**（宣告式的多 tab/多 pane workspace 範本 + 模糊選擇器——`tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` 的對應物）與 **Quick Actions**（模糊指令 launcher——彈出選單的對應物）。

**安裝已自動化**，由 `devtools` ansible role（`# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` 區塊）處理——冪等、每次 `chezmoi apply` 都會跑、裝好後就跳過。它呼叫：

```bash
herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # 手動 fallback / role 實際跑的東西
```

`herdr plugin install` **在沒有 Go toolchain 時會下載預編譯 release binary**，所以有沒有 Go 都能用。唯一的陷阱：若 `PATH` 上有一個*過期*的 Go（例如舊的 `/usr/local/go` 遮蔽了較新的），herdr 會嘗試從原始碼建置並失敗（`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`），而不是 fallback。ansible task 透過在可用時把 mise 的 Go（`mise which go` → 它的 bin 目錄）前置到 PATH 來規避；手動修法：把現代 Go 放前面：`PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`。（Go 現在由 mise 管理，受 `installExtraRuntimes` gate。）

Projects 範本由 chezmoi 管理於 `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → `~/.config/` 下的同一路徑。內建的 `chezmoi.toml` 對應本 repo 的 tmuxinator `chezmoi` session（editor/git/shell tab）。把 `prefix+O` 綁到 Projects、`prefix+y` 綁到 Quick Actions（設定裡已備好）。

**Quick Actions** 同樣由 chezmoi 管理，位於 `…/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/`（每個 action 一個 TOML）。本 repo 出貨六個 **copy** action（見 [複製 pane 與 space 的資訊](#copy-to-clipboard)）,外加 plugin 的五個**起手式**範例（GitHub / Google / Search Google / Open Repo / Reveal Working Dir）,已為 Linux 調整——macOS `open` → 本 repo 的跨平台 [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md),repo 選單指向 `daviddwlee84/*`。這些 copy 操作刻意集中在此處,不再占用六個 prefix 直達鍵。因為這個受管目錄非空,herdr-plus **不會** 自己 seed 那些範例（它只在*空*目錄時 seed）,所以在此 vendored;不要的 TOML 刪掉即可。要新增就往這裡丟一個 TOML,或在 `<repo>/.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` 出貨一組 repo 本地的。

> **Quick Actions 是給一次性、非互動式指令用的**（內建範例全是 `open <url>`）。herdr-plus 用 `sh -c` 跑選中的 action,沒有 PTY、沒有互動 stdin,所以互動式 TUI 會出問題——btop 立刻退出、nvtop 收不到 F10。要跑 TUI 就用 dev/lazygit 那種*浮動 command pane*（`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`）——這就是為何 **dev**（`prefix+d`）、**btop**（`prefix+M`）與 **nvtop**（`prefix+N`）是快捷鍵而非 Quick Action。

## Television 整合 {#television-integration}
## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)

[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).

**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:

```bash
herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
```

`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)

Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).

**Quick Actions** are chezmoi-managed alongside them, under `…/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` (one TOML per action). The repo ships the six **copy** actions (see [Copy pane + space facts](#copy-to-clipboard)) plus the plugin's five **starter** examples (GitHub / Google / Search Google / Open Repo / Reveal Working Dir), adapted for Linux — macOS `open` → the repo's cross-platform [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md), and the repo-select points at `daviddwlee84/*`. The copy operations deliberately live here instead of consuming six direct prefix keys. Because this managed dir is non-empty, herdr-plus does **not** auto-seed those examples itself (it only seeds into an *empty* dir), which is why they're vendored here; delete any TOML you don't want. Add your own by dropping a TOML here, or ship a repo-local set in `<repo>/.herdr-plus/quick-actions/`.

> **Quick Actions are for one-off, non-interactive commands** (the shipped examples all `open <url>`). herdr-plus runs a chosen action via `sh -c` with no PTY and no interactive stdin, so an interactive TUI misbehaves — btop exits immediately, nvtop can't receive F10. For a TUI you want the dev/lazygit-style *floating command pane* (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) instead — that's why **dev** (`prefix+d`), **btop** (`prefix+M`), and **nvtop** (`prefix+N`) are keybinds, not Quick Actions.
````

Everything is in place and live on this machine: `chezmoi apply` ran for herdr, `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`, and herdr reloaded the config with no warnings. I haven't committed anything.

**On your screenshot:** Quick Actions can do two levels, but not deeper. Level 1 is the action list and level 2 is that action's option list. In the herdr-plus source, an option has no nested options, though it can be a grey group heading. So I laid it out like this:

- **Level 1:** press `prefix+y` and type `agent` to filter down to five entries: `Agent: Claude Code`, `Codex`, `OpenCode`, `Claude (Copilot, once)` and `Codex (Copilot, once)`.
- **Level 2:** a list grouped under a **SpecStory (record)** heading and a **Direct** heading, each with → Split right / ↓ Split down / ⊞ New tab.
  - OpenCode only shows Direct, because SpecStory doesn't support it.
  - The two Copilot entries pass your choice as `--specstory-mode run|off`.

**Hotkeys:**
- `prefix+Alt+c`: claude + SpecStory, split right
- `prefix+Alt+x`: codex + SpecStory, split right
- `prefix+Alt+t`: claude + SpecStory, new tab
- `prefix+Alt+r`: repeat your last choice, whether it came from a hotkey or the menu

**Why it's faster:**
- herdr can only open a new pane with your default shell, so `agent-open.sh` passes the choice to it in an environment variable.
- A few lines at the very top of `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`, before oh-my-zsh and ble.sh load, see that variable. They start the agent straight away with a minimal environment: PATH, editor, mise and your secrets files.
- When you quit the agent, the rest of the shell loads normally, so the pane becomes an ordinary shell.
- Only the five known agent names and two modes are accepted; nothing from the variable is executed as a command.

**Verified:**
- A real OpenCode launch was detected about 1s after running the launcher, in the right directory.
- A pane opened with a bogus agent name triggered the guard, which rejected the name.
- `zsh -i` and `bash -i` start normally when the variable isn't set.
- Even with a stripped-down PATH, the minimal environment finds claude, codex, opencode, specstory and node, plus both copilot-once functions.
- The new test file `tests/unit/herdr_agent_open.bats` passes all 13 tests, including a check that every menu option is valid for the launcher.

**Caveats:**
- **Hotkeys not pressed yet:** I couldn't press the four `prefix+Alt` keys from here. The config reloads cleanly, and if the key doesn't pass the pane's directory, the script asks herdr for it instead. Still worth one manual press each.
- **zsh secrets not loaded:** the fast path skips `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`. If an agent needs something from it, set `HERDR_AGENT_FULL_RC=1` to use the old, slower full-shell path.
- **Docs build fails, but not because of this change:** `just docs-build` fails on this Mac because of the known libcairo problem. It fails the same way with my changes stashed.

I also added docs in English and zh-TW (`docs/tools/herdr.md` § Open a coding agent), a line in `docs/shells/keybindings.md`, and a mention in the agent skill template. Want me to commit?

**On your question: yes. It only takes effect when a pane is opened through the Quick Actions or the four new hotkeys. Normal use isn't affected.**

- **Shell startup:** the only change is the small block at the top of `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`. It does nothing unless the `HERDR_AGENT_LAUNCH` variable is set. Only `agent-open.sh` sets it, and only on the new pane it creates. When the variable is absent, it's a single empty check. I confirmed `zsh -i` and `bash -i` start normally.
- **No spreading to other shells:** the block clears the variable before starting the agent. Shells the agent opens later, other panes, and new tabs never see it.
- **Manual splits and tabs:** `prefix+v`, `prefix+c` and the mouse "+" don't set the variable, so they behave exactly as before.
- **Hotkeys:** only four were added, `prefix+Alt+c/x/t/r`. All were unused before, and herdr reported no key conflicts on reload. Your existing herdr keys are unchanged.
- **Quick Actions:** the list has five extra `Agent: …` entries. The existing translate and copy actions are unchanged.
- **The one difference to keep in mind:** an agent started this way gets the lean environment (PATH, editor, mise, your secrets files) rather than everything your shell loads. Anything that exists only in `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh` won't reach that agent. After you quit the agent, the pane loads your full shell as usual.

順便想問一下 類似 prefix + G 那種 lazygit 的啟動方式 直接跑agent binary vs. 在簡化init的zsh跑 什麼區別？

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-14 05:27:40Z)**_

兩種都不用載入完整的 zsh，速度幾乎一樣。真正的差別在 **pane 的生命週期**和**環境從哪裡來**。

| | `prefix+G` 式（`type = "pane"`，直接跑 binary） | 我們的做法（新 pane 的 shell 先跑 agent） |
|---|---|---|
| pane 裡的根行程 | agent 本身 | zsh，agent 是它的子行程 |
| agent 結束後 | **pane 直接消失** | pane 留下來，接著載完整 zsh，變成一般 shell |
| 誤按 Ctrl+C／agent crash | 畫面和錯誤訊息跟著 pane 一起不見 | 還能看到輸出，可以直接 `claude --resume` |
| 位置 | herdr 固定的右側 50/50 暫時 pane（會 zoom，`sidecar.sh` 還得手動取消 zoom） | 右、下、新 tab 都可以選，還能貼上 label |
| 環境 | herdr **server 啟動當下**凍結的 env，不跑任何 rc | `agent-run.sh` 每次重新組：PATH、mise（依 cwd）、secrets |
| `claude-copilot-once` 這類 shell function | 不能直接用，要另寫 wrapper | 可以，會 source `43_copilot_proxy.sh` |
| 觸發方式 | 只能綁快捷鍵（Quick Actions 沒有 PTY，開不了這種 pane） | Quick Actions 和快捷鍵都能用 |
| 速度 | 最快 | 多一個 login zsh 加精簡 init，約 0.1 秒；跟 agent 本身約 1 秒的啟動比，幾乎感覺不到 |

**為什麼「server 凍結的 env」是實際的風險**

herdr 的 pane env 是 server 啟動時就定下來的（docs 的 Keybindings 段落有寫）。所以 server 開著的期間：

- 改了 secrets、裝了新版 agent、mise 換了版本，直接跑的 agent 都看不到。
- per-project 的 mise 設定也不會套用，因為沒人依 cwd 跑 `mise env`。

我們的做法每次開 pane 都重新讀這些，所以不受影響。

**什麼時候直接跑比較好**

lazygit、btop 這類「用完就關」的工具，正好適合讓 pane 跟著消失，而且它們不需要 secrets 或 mise。agent 剛好相反：它是會長時間跑的工作 session，退出後通常還想留著那個位置（看輸出、resume、跑 git），所以用 shell 墊底比較合適。

**折衷做法**

如果某個情境你就是想要「關掉就消失」，可以加一個 `type = "pane"` 的鍵，`command = "~/.config/herdr/agent-run.sh claude run"`。這樣直接跑我們的 runner，不經過 zsh，環境照樣會重新組，copilot-once 也能用。代價是位置固定在右側暫時 pane，退出後 pane 就關掉。要的話我可以幫你加一個。
